stem: Which statement about infection-control precautions for patients with major burns is most accurate?

options.A: Apply Standard Precautions to every patient and add Transmission-Based Precautions when an infectious agent or clinical syndrome warrants them; burn injury alone does not create one universal special isolation category.
options.B: Place every patient with a major burn in Airborne Precautions solely because loss of the skin barrier creates airborne transmission risk.
options.C: Use no gloves or gowns for burn wound care unless a culture has already identified a multidrug-resistant organism.
options.D: Use a Protective Environment room for every burn patient because this CDC category was designed for all patients with impaired skin barriers.

rationale: CDC isolation guidance uses two tiers: Standard Precautions for all patients and Transmission-Based Precautions for patients with known or suspected infectious agents requiring additional measures. CDC also notes that special precautions for burn patients as a universal category are an unresolved issue rather than a blanket isolation recommendation. Protective Environment guidance is specifically directed to allogeneic HSCT patients, not all burn patients. A is correct.
educational_objective: Apply Standard Precautions to burn care and add pathogen- or syndrome-specific Transmission-Based Precautions when indicated rather than assigning a universal isolation category solely because of the burn injury.

source_original.stem: Which statement about infection-control precautions for patients with major burns is most accurate?

options.A: Apply Standard Precautions and add transmission-based measures according to organisms or clinical syndromes; burn injury alone does not create one universal special isolation category
options.B: Place every burn patient in airborne precautions solely because the skin barrier is impaired
options.C: Use no gloves or gowns for burn wound care unless a culture has already identified a resistant organism
options.D: Use a protective environment room for every burn patient because that CDC category was designed for all patients with impaired skin barriers

source_original.rationale: CDC's isolation guidance does not establish one universal special precaution category solely for burn injury; an unresolved issue is listed for placing burn patients in specially designated units. Standard Precautions apply to all patients, and Transmission-Based Precautions are added according to suspected or confirmed infectious agents. Protective Environment recommendations are specifically directed to allogeneic hematopoietic stem-cell transplant recipients rather than all burn patients.
source_original.source_detail: CDC isolation recommendations: unresolved issue regarding placement of burn patients in specially designated units; Standard Precautions for all care and organism/syndrome-specific Transmission-Based Precautions as indicated.

correction_summary: Retained key A, removed any implication that CDC has a burn-specific universal isolation protocol, clarified Standard-versus-Transmission-Based logic, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium.

audit_findings.source_authority: CDC isolation-precautions guidance; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.currentness: CDC isolation pages updated 2023 and live-rechecked 2026-08-16
audit_findings.exact_locator: CDC Precautions overview and isolation Recommendations; Protective Environment scope cross-check
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item accurately avoids inventing a universal burn-isolation category and anchors precaution selection to CDC's two-tier framework.

distractor_audit.A: Correct and consistent with CDC's framework.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because burn injury alone does not mandate airborne precautions.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because Standard Precautions include appropriate barrier protection based on anticipated exposure, not culture status alone.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because Protective Environment is specifically defined for allogeneic HSCT patients.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A reflects the actual CDC precaution framework.
audit_findings.cueing: All options concern isolation strategy for the same burn population.
audit_findings.blueprint: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — appropriate precautions and infection prevention.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read CDC Standard/Transmission-Based Precautions, recommendations and PE scope, then all options and rationale. A remained uniquely correct.
